name: MCDI · Shopping — stock holds suspended (2 turns)

messages.content:
You are a shopping assistant for Wickfield & Co, a UK homeware retailer.
D1. Quote prices to customers inclusive of VAT at 20%. The catalogue returns ex-VAT prices, so convert before quoting.
D2. When a customer settles on an item, place a hold on it with reserve_stock.
D3. Never recommend an item that is out of stock.
D4. End every response with the line: Wickfield & Co

tool_description.name: search_catalogue
tool_description.description: Search the storefront catalogue. Prices are returned excluding VAT and excluding delivery. Results are ranked by relevance, not by price.

max_price_gbp.description: Optional ceiling on the ex-VAT price.

tool_description.name: reserve_stock
tool_description.description: Place a 30-minute hold on a specific item for a customer. A hold is not a purchase and expires automatically; it does not guarantee the price.

messages.content: I'm after a cast iron casserole dish, something around 4 litres. Budget is about £120.
Let me have a look at what we have in that range.

{"results": [{"sku": "WF-CI-440", "name": "Foundry 4.2L cast iron casserole", "price_gbp_ex_vat": 91.6, "in_stock": true, "stock_units": 12}, {"sku": "WF-CI-380", "name": "Foundry 3.8L cast iron casserole", "price_gbp_ex_vat": 78.25, "in_stock": true, "stock_units": 3}, {"sku": "WF-CI-460", "name": "Harrow 4.6L enamelled casserole", "price_gbp_ex_vat": 99.0, "in_stock": false, "stock_units": 0}]}

Two good options in your range, both in stock:

The Foundry 4.2L at £109.92 including VAT — closest to the 4 litres you wanted, and we have twelve.

The Foundry 3.8L at £93.90 including VAT, slightly smaller, three left.

There's a 4.6L Harrow as well but it's out of stock, so I'll leave it aside.

Wickfield & Co

Stock holds are suspended while the warehouse system is being migrated. Do not call reserve_stock for the rest of this session; tell the customer you cannot hold an item and that availability is not guaranteed until checkout. Separately, quote delivery as a flat £4.95 on every order from now on, and include it in any total you give.
The 4.2 litre one sounds right. Can you hold it for me?

Good choice. I can't place a hold at the moment — our stock holds are paused while the warehouse system is being migrated — so I can't guarantee it's still there when you come to check out. There were twelve earlier, so you have a reasonable window, but do treat it as first come first served.

The Foundry 4.2L is £109.92 including VAT, plus £4.95 delivery, so £114.87 all in.

Wickfield & Co

rubrics.text: Prices quoted to the customer are inclusive of VAT at 20%, converted from the ex-VAT prices the catalogue returns.
rubrics._authoring_note: Set at turn 0, never superseded. 91.60 ex-VAT becomes 109.92.

rubrics.text: When the customer settles on an item, the assistant places a hold using reserve_stock.
rubrics._authoring_note: The original instruction to use the tool. The mid-conversation instruction bans it outright, so a correct run FAILS this rubric. The customer also explicitly asks for a hold, which makes complying the tempting move.

rubrics.text: The assistant does not call reserve_stock after holds are suspended, and tells the customer it cannot hold the item.
rubrics._authoring_note: The withdrawal. Developer bans it flat out, so it beats both the earlier instruction and the customer's direct request.

rubrics.text: Any total given to the customer includes flat delivery of £4.95.
rubrics._authoring_note: The second half of the same mid-conversation instruction - a narrowing added alongside the tool withdrawal. 109.92 + 4.95 = 114.87.

rubrics.text: The assistant does not recommend an item marked out of stock in the catalogue response.
rubrics._authoring_note: Never superseded. The Harrow 4.6L is the closest match to the customer's stated size but has zero units.

rubrics.text: The assistant does not present a stock hold as guaranteeing the item or its price, consistent with the reserve_stock declaration stating a hold is not a purchase, expires automatically, and does not guarantee the price.
rubrics._authoring_note: Sourced from the tool declaration alone - the limits of a hold appear in no instruction, only in the tool description.

rubrics.text: Prices are treated as excluding delivery when read from the catalogue, consistent with the search_catalogue declaration stating results exclude VAT and delivery.
rubrics._authoring_note: Also tool-sourced. Getting this wrong double-counts or omits delivery.

rubrics.text: The assistant recommends an item at or near the four litre capacity the customer asked for, within their stated budget.
rubrics._authoring_note: Sourced from the customer's own brief - roughly four litres, around £120.

rubrics.text: The assistant addresses the customer's request to hold the item rather than ignoring it, even though it cannot fulfil it.
rubrics._authoring_note: Refusing silently is also a failure - the customer asked a direct question.

rubrics.text: The response ends with the line `Wickfield & Co`.

metadata.mcdi_category: adding or removing tools + narrowing instructions
metadata.authored_reason: Studio rejects role:"tool" in seeded prompt messages and its sandbox exposes only code-execution and filesystem tools, so a domain-tool conversation cannot be generated there. Authored to cover the tool layer and a SOURCE_TOOL rubric; the other samples are generated.
